title: Emotional Intelligence and Communication Skills in Healthcare University Students: The Mediating Role of Interpersonal Skills
content: High-quality healthcare demands soft skills alongside technical knowledge. While critical for managing clinical anxiety, the specific pathways linking emotional intelligence (EI), interpersonal skills (IS), and communication skills (CS) remain under-researched. This study analyzes the predictive and mediational role of IS between EI and CS in healthcare undergraduates. A quantitative, cross-sectional study was conducted with 816 healthcare students. Data from four standardized self-reports were analyzed using a structural equa-tion model estimated via Unweighted Least Squares. The structural model showed a highly satisfactory fit. EI positively predicted IS (β= 0.69) and directly predicted CS (β = 0.35). Crucially, IS strongly predicted CS (β = 0.69), acting as a key psychological mediator. Within EI, Emotional Clarity (0.61) and Repair (0.59) were the strongest predictors. For so-cial competencies, Assertiveness was the strongest positive indicator (β = 0.85), while Ef-fective Social Interaction showed an inverse load (β = -0.93), functioning as a protective mechanism against social anxiety. Together, EI and IS explained 91% of the variance in communication skills (R2 = 0.91). IS structurally mediate the link between internal emo-tional regulation and communication efficiency. Healthcare training must move beyond basic communication protocols to integrate formal EI and social skills programs.
